newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain Unions call protest over public wage freeze.
newsitem.headline: Spain Unions call protest over public wage freeze.

text.p: Spanish unions on Monday took the first step towards a possible general strike when they agreed on two days of demonstrations against a public sector wage freeze confirmed by the government last week.

The public sector syndicates, which include Spain's two largest unions, Workers' Commissions (CCOO) and the General Workers' Union (UGT), agreed to stage joint protests on September 30 and October 15.

"The arguments the government often relies on to justify a salary freeze are fallacies," said Enrique Alonso, spokesman for the Confederation of Independent Unions and Public Sector Unions (CSIF). "Maastricht does not justify a wage freeze."
A spokesman for CCOO last week said the October 15 action could be followed by a general strike of one or two days. Unions will meet again on October 17 to discuss the issue.

The conservative government of Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar on Thursday confirmed it would freeze public sector salaries in 1997 to help whip Spain into shape for Europe's single currency. The government aims to save up to 180 billions pesetas with this measure.

Unions have been warning since early summer that they could stage mass protests against the wage freeze, which breaks a labour accord reached with the former Socialist administration guaranteeing wage rises in 1997 in line with inflation.
